title: Union, the Trianon, the Liberty and the Strand
summary: After joining the union and losing the job, she plays the Trianon, then the Sanger Liberty and Strand; organ and orchestra alternate.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: It worked. It worked. So, anyway, that's from that. I, I, uh, oh, the union was involved. And, and, uh, I did join the union. And then, Fichtenberg, I think, got angry with the union. And fired everybody that was union. And then across the street, on Canal, where, about where, um, where, uh, God Show is, was a picture show owned by Pierce Company. I don't know whether it was a company or not Pierce, anyway. And it was the Trianon. So, I, I got the job playing the organ, real sure enough, organ over there. And, uh, played there. Uh, actually, I don't remember until I went to work for Sanger then. And they had a show up on, uh, St. Charles, the Liberty, I believe was the name of it.
Where, um, Max Fink had an orchestra up there. Yes.
And they had a big organ.
Well, I played there, because I don't remember how long at all.
Was that where the orchestra, or a solo?

No, uh, organ, uh, played when the orchestra was not playing. I see. Uh, but sometimes, uh, once in a great while, a picture that came out would have a score with it. And there might, might be some time in that way you, you, you played as the orchestra did. I don't remember that that was done at, uh, at, um, the Liberty. But, uh, it did, uh, later, uh, uh, when the Strand opened up and got the main to direct the Greek orchestra that they had named Don Filippini, uh, we also would, well, occasionally would have a score, you know, so that, just once in a while, we played at the same time.
